patch.value: The publish-attestation scan judged shell text with a regular expression, so real unattested publishes scanned clean

The guard decided whether any publish omits provenance by blanking quoted spans and splitting the remainder on three operators. Blanking deletes the very argument under audit, so a publish carrying an attestation reads as one without it, and the reverse is worse: an eval or a bash dash-c wrapping a publish disappears from the scan entirely, leaving an attested sibling elsewhere in the file to carry the audit to green. The operator split also misses a backgrounding ampersand, a pipe written without surrounding spaces, and command substitution. Replaced by a real tokeniser that resolves what each command actually runs.

value.author: claude
value.text: Extracted scripts/shell-command-scan.ts: a tokeniser that tracks single, double and backslash quoting per character while keeping the quoted text in the token, splits on the full operator set (semicolon, ampersand, double-ampersand, pipe, double-pipe, newline) regardless of surrounding whitespace, and unwraps interpreter shells so that eval and bash dash-c bodies are re-scanned as commands rather than swallowed as string arguments. The attestation guard now asks the tokeniser for command name and arguments instead of pattern-matching text. Covered to 100/100/100/100; test/coverage-gate.test.ts stub updated to enumerate the new source file, which the gate requires.

value.author: claude
value.text: Adversarially measured, not reasoned about. Fourteen bypass shapes drawn from the Greptile findings raised across the fleet were run against the tokeniser: global options before the subcommand, a quoted subcommand, a quoted flag, eval, bash -c, a combined short-option cluster (bash -ec), sh -c, a pipe without surrounding spaces, a single backgrounding ampersand, command substitution, backticks, an env prefix, a subshell, and a package runner. Thirteen were already caught; npx was not, so package runners and their own option words are now consumed as wrappers. A second round found the two-word runners (pnpm dlx, yarn exec, bun x) still escaping, and those are consumed only when the second word completes the pair, so an unrelated pnpm install is not re-pointed at its first argument. Both new rules were revert-checked: removing either drops the suite from 40 passing to a failure.

value.author: claude
value.text: Propagating the guard to the fleet exposed that it was not self-contained: it imported six shared symbols from the changelog-date gate, a file only four of the sixteen packages have. The dependency also pointed the wrong way, an attestation gate reaching into a changelog gate for shell-text helpers. The shell-text helpers and the two shared gate shapes now live in shell-command-scan.ts, and isMainInvocation moved to scripts/main-invocation.ts, which is the factoring pm-beads had already arrived at independently and whose realpath comparison also recognises a symlinked entry point. Both gates now depend on the shared modules rather than on each other.

value.author: claude
value.text: Propagation surfaced a coverage-locality defect. The shared scanner's branches were exercised only through the changelog-date gate's suite, so copying the scanner into a package that has no such gate dropped a branch (the fallback in expandArrays that leaves an undeclared array reference in place) and the coverage gate failed there rather than in the package that owns the module. The scanner and the main-invocation guard now carry test/shell-command-scan.test.ts, which travels with them; the two assertions that genuinely test the date gate's integration stayed in that gate's suite, so nothing is tested twice.

value.author: claude
value.text: Greptile found two more bypasses in the tokeniser after the convergence landed, both correct and both in code written this session. First, a wrapper option that takes a separate value moved the program past where the scan looks: sudo dash u root npm publish resolved root as the executable and the publish vanished. Enumerating which options of which wrapper take a value would be a list that goes stale silently, and each omission is a missed publish, so the fix is at the auditing layer instead: once a wrapper has been consumed every later word is also offered as a possible program. That direction costs noise and never a miss, which is the right trade for a gate whose failure mode is an unattested release. Second, a token-wide quoted flag could not tell an assignment apart from a literal that looks like one, so NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY equals a quoted URL followed by npm publish read the assignment itself as the program. Tokens now record whether their FIRST character was quoted, which is exactly the distinction the shell makes. Both revert-checked: restoring either drops the suite from 42 passing to a failure. Twenty-four adversarial shapes now pass, up from fourteen.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round three of Greptile findings, and my own first test of them was itself vacuous, which is worth recording. Feeding each bypass to the gate on its own showed every one caught; they were caught by the non-vacuity guard reporting that no publish was found anywhere, not by detecting the unattested one. That is precisely the failure the gate exists to prevent, reproduced in its own test harness. Re-run with an ordinary attested publish beside each candidate, ten of the twelve claims were real. Fixed: a redirection and its target are not command words, so an operator written before the command no longer reads as the program, and a file-descriptor duplication such as two-greater-than-ampersand-one is one word rather than a backgrounding separator; the shell keywords if, then, else, elif, while, until, do, negation and an opening brace or paren introduce a command rather than being one; npm exec and npm x join the two-word runner set alongside pnpm dlx; and a command held in a quoted scalar is expanded from its assignment, because the assignment is where the command actually is. One claim was refused with evidence rather than fixed: eval with a split payload is not a bypass, since the shell joins an evaluator's words with a space, so eval of npm-space-pub and lish runs npm pub lish, which bash confirms installs a package called lish rather than publishing anything. Forty-five adversarial shapes now pass and no attested form produces a false failure. Each of the three fixes is revert-checked individually.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round four, and the round-three change I made broke every package in the fleet before this landed. Expanding any quoted assignment inlined values such as a package name captured from a command substitution, which injected an unbalanced parenthesis into unrelated commands: the scan then reported a publish that does not exist while losing the attested one that does, and all sixteen release gates failed on their own workflow. Only a plain literal value is inlined now, one carrying a substitution, a backtick, a parenthesis or a quote of its own is left alone, and the variable-held-command bypass this was written for is still caught. A regression test pins it, using the exact shape that broke: a package name captured from a substitution, a publish mentioned in a comment, and the real attested invocation, asserting exactly one finding and the right one. Four further Greptile findings fixed in this round: a YAML key carries the command as its value so run colon npm publish is a publish; a quoted parenthesis inside a substitution is a literal rather than its delimiter; one package script cannot continue into the next through a trailing backslash; and npm selects a workspace with a flag, so listing workspace as a runner subcommand only meant a publish written after it was never audited.
